exam_name: Praxis Core: Academic Skills for Educators - Mathematics

domains.name: Data Interpretation and Representation, Statistics, and Probability

aliases: Praxis Core: Academic Skills for Educators - Mathematics

editorial.meta_description: Prepare for the Praxis Core Mathematics exam with 56 questions covering number and quantity, statistics, algebra, and geometry over a specific time limit.
editorial.overview: The Praxis Core: Academic Skills for Educators - Mathematics exam, administered by ETS, evaluates college and career readiness in quantitative reasoning for prospective educators. Over a timed 90-minute testing session, test takers complete exactly 56 questions spanning number and quantity, data interpretation and statistics, and algebra and geometry to prove their foundational teaching competencies.
editorial.who_should_take: This exam is intended for candidates preparing for a career in education who need to demonstrate quantitative skills required for educator preparation programs and teacher certification.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review arithmetic, algebraic procedures, and geometric formulas carefully before test day. Practice solving multi-step word problems, working with various data displays, and calculating statistical measures. Familiarize yourself well with the provided on-screen four-function calculator to manage your time effectively during the complete 90-minute testing session.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers integers, decimals, fractions, ratios, proportions, percents, and constant rates. It assumes a solid knowledge of basic U.S. customary and metric systems of measurement for solving daily quantitative problems.
study_focus: Solve problems involving integers, decimals, and fractions
Solve problems involving ratios and proportions

domain_guidance.summary: This domain assesses the ability to read and interpret visual displays of quantitative information accurately, compute various measures of central tendency, and assign simple mathematical probabilities to events.
study_focus: Work with data and data representations to solve problems
Solve problems involving measures of central tendency and spread
Use data from a random sample to draw inferences
Compute simple probabilities and use them to solve problems

domain_guidance.summary: This specific section focuses heavily on manipulating algebraic expressions, following standard mathematical procedures, solving complex word problems and equations, and successfully applying basic geometric properties and relevant formulas to complete problems.
study_focus: Use properties of operations to identify or generate equivalent algebraic expressions
Solve word problems involving linear relationships
Utilize basic properties of common two-dimensional shapes
Use formulas for area, circumference, perimeter, and volume

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive fully prepared for a computer-delivered test featuring exactly 56 questions. An on-screen four-function calculator is provided during the complete 90-minute testing session for all registered candidates.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The exam contains exactly 56 questions in total, which include both scored operational items and unscored pretest questions distributed across three distinct content domains for educators.
The official passing score for the exam varies significantly by state and certifying agency. You should always check directly with ETS or your local certification office for specific requirements.
The exam is exactly 90 minutes long in total duration and is delivered entirely via computer at designated testing centers for all registered candidates seeking certification.
An on-screen four-function calculator is officially provided directly within the testing software interface during the test for all test takers to use for calculations during the session.

methodology.summary: This detailed overview was built carefully using official ETS exam guides, official testing documentation, and verified resource materials for the Praxis Core Mathematics test.
